ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, the horizontal plane is tangent to a semicircular track with radius $R$ in the vertical plane at point $B$. An object with mass $m$ compresses a spring to a distance of $3R$ from point $B$ at position $A$ and is released from rest. The object slides to the right along the horizontal plane, detaches from the spring after some time, and enters the semicircular track at point $B$ with a normal force of $8mg$ exerted on the track. It then passes through the highest point $C$ of the circular track with a velocity of $\sqrt{g R}$. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the horizontal plane is 0.5, and air resistance is negligible. Find:

1. What is the magnitude of the centripetal force on the object at point $B$?
2. What is the displacement of the object's motion after leaving point $C$?
3. What is the work done by the spring force on the object?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
$7mg$
$2\sqrt{2}R$, at an angle of $45^{\circ}$ to the horizontal, diagonally downward to the left.
$5mgR$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the left side is a fixed wall and a compressed spring, and the right end of the spring contacts a small block, whose initial position is labeled A; between A and the entrance B of the circular-arc track on the right is a horizontal surface. On the right is a semicircular track in a vertical plane, and the horizontal surface is tangent to the circular track at point B; the figure labels the center O and radius R, and the highest point of the track is labeled C. Therefore according to the diagram, B can be regarded as the lowest point of the circular track, and C as the highest point. Reasoning: 1. At point B, the radial direction pointing toward the center O is vertically upward. The magnitude of the normal force of the track on the object is 8mg, directed upward; gravity mg is downward. Therefore the net radial force at point B is N - mg = 8mg - mg = 7mg, and this is the magnitude of the centripetal force. Therefore F_c,B = 7mg. At the same time, m v_B^2/R = 7mg can be obtained, namely v_B^2 = 7gR. 2. After the object passes the highest point C, it leaves the track, and its velocity is along the tangent direction of the track. From the semicircular-track relation in the figure, the height of point C relative to the horizontal surface is 2R; at point C the tangent direction is horizontally to the left, and the speed is given as v_C = sqrt(gR). After leaving C, it undergoes horizontal projectile motion, falling 2R in the vertical direction: 2R = (1/2) g t^2, giving t = 2 sqrt(R/g). The magnitude of the horizontal displacement is x = v_C t = sqrt(gR) · 2 sqrt(R/g) = 2R, directed to the left; the vertical displacement is 2R, directed downward. Therefore the magnitude of the total displacement is sqrt((2R)^2 + (2R)^2) = 2sqrt(2)R, and the direction is at a 45° angle with the horizontal, obliquely downward to the left. 3. Use the work-energy theorem from A to B. The object is released from rest at A, the distance from A to B is 3R, and the coefficient of kinetic friction on the horizontal surface is μ = 0.5, so the work done by friction is W_f = -μmg·3R = -0.5mg·3R = -1.5mgR. The kinetic energy at point B is K_B = (1/2)m v_B^2 = (1/2)m·7gR = 3.5mgR. Let the work done by the spring force be W_s, then W_s + W_f = K_B - 0 = 3.5mgR, so W_s = 3.5mgR + 1.5mgR = 5mgR.
